newsitem.title: USA: US DOE awards $54 mln in Hanford Site contracts.
newsitem.headline: US DOE awards $54 mln in Hanford Site contracts.

text.p: The U.S. Energy Department Wednesday said it awarded two $27 million contracts -- one to Lockheed Martin Advanced Environmental Systems, a division of Lockheed Corp, and one to BNFL Inc -- to treat and stabilize radioactive waste at the Hanford Site in Washington.

Based on the companies' performances on these contracts, the department said it will decide whether to authorize one or both contractors to proceed with a contract valued at $5 billion or more and expected to take 10 to 14 years to complete.

The BNFL Inc teams included Bechtel National Inc, GTS Duratek and SAIC. The Lockheed team is comprised of M4 Environmental L.P., Fluor Daniel Inc , Numatec, Duke Engineering and Services Inc, Babcock and Wilcox, Nukem Nuclear Technologies Corp, Los Alamos Technical Associates Inc, AEA Technology and OHM Remediation Services Corp.
The contracts were to solidify as much as 14 million gallons of radioactive and chemical wastes in the 177 tanks at the former nuclear weapons site.
The department said this is a 20-month project to establish technical, operational, regulatoray, business and financial elements required by privatized tank treatment facilities.

The next phase would be a commercial demonstration project designed to treat six to 13 percent of the tank wastes at Hanford on a fixed unit price basis, a contract with an estimated $5 billion or more value.

The Energy Department said the contracts were part of its initiative to increasingly privatize work at the nation's largest environmental cleanup project. With it, contractors finance and build the cleanup facilities, and the department pays only for the solidified waste.
